title: Announcing Holiday Hours So Nobody Is Surprised
seoTitle: Announcing Holiday Hours So Nobody Gets Surprised
excerpt: National Day 2026 hands most teams four days off in a row. Here is where to post the hours, when, and the exact template that stops the same complaint from landing four times.
seoDescription: National Day 2026 falls 25 to 26 November, creating a four day close. Learn where to post holiday hours and the template that stops complaints.

blocks.text: National Day 2026 falls on Wednesday and Thursday, 25 and 26 November. Add the Friday Saturday weekend either side and most businesses face four straight days of closed or shortened hours, from Wednesday morning to Saturday night. Every one of those four days, someone will call, message or walk up to your door not knowing that.
The four days everyone will ask about

segments.text: The Ministry of Labour confirmed National Day for 2026 as 25 and 26 November back in December, part of a new policy of announcing the year's national and religious holidays months in advance. That means a hotel, a polyclinic or a dealership has had nearly a year's notice, which removes the excuse for a last-minute scramble.
It does not remove the work. Someone still has to decide the actual hours for those four days and then put that decision everywhere a customer might look.

Some businesses will close fully. Others will run a skeleton front desk, keep a clinic's urgent line open, or shift a dealership's service bay to appointment only. Whatever you choose, the decision is only useful once it reaches the people asking.
A confused customer does not read a memo. They check whichever channel is fastest for them, often more than one, and they trust the first answer they find, even if it is wrong.

items.text: Google Business Profile: the hours line under your name in search results, which most people check before they call anyone
WhatsApp: the business hours field and the automatic away message, if your WhatsApp is where enquiries already pile up
The phone greeting or IVR message: the recording or menu a caller hears before anyone speaks to them
The door: a printed sign with both the closing date and the exact reopening date, not just "closed for holiday"

segments.text: Miss one of these four and you have not really announced anything. A caller who hears an old greeting will not think to check Google. A walk-up guest reading a door sign will not think to check WhatsApp.
If WhatsApp already carries most of your enquiry traffic, treat it as seriously as the phone line itself.

blocks.text: A holiday hours announcement only works if it reaches every channel a customer might check, not just the one you remembered first.
When to post it, and in which languages

segments.text: Google's own guidance for special hours is to set them as soon as you know the dates, ideally a week or two ahead, so the change appears before the search traffic does. WhatsApp business hours and the away message can go up the same week. The door sign and the phone greeting are the two people forget, because updating a recording feels like a bigger job than it is.

blocks.caption: A four-day timeline that works for most service teams
rows: Google Business Profile special hours, WhatsApp business hours
Phone greeting or IVR message, printed door sign
WhatsApp away message switched on, final check of all four channels
Greeting and away message reverted to normal hours

segments.text: Arabic and English cover most callers. If your usual customers include workers or guests who read Hindi or Urdu on your door sign, a third line costs almost nothing to add and prevents the most common walk-up complaint: someone who could not read the sign at all.

blocks.text: What an unannounced weekend actually costs

segments.text: Here is a composite estimate for a 12-line polyclinic call desk that leaves its Google hours, WhatsApp status and phone greeting untouched over the National Day weekend. Run the same maths on your own call volumes and rates.

blocks.caption: Composite example: cost of a silent holiday hours page over four days
rows: Confused calls answered by voicemail or a bewildered on-call staff member (15 calls a day x 4 days)
60 calls, 3 minutes of staff time each
Appointments lost to patients who assumed the clinic was fully closed and rebooked elsewhere (3 patients)
3 x average consultation margin of OMR 12
One negative Google review from a caller who reached a closed door, costing two future enquiries at an average booking value of OMR 15
Staff overtime the following morning clearing the backlog (2 hours)

segments.text: Compare that to the cost of doing it properly: a printed sign for under OMR 5, a Google and WhatsApp update that takes fifteen minutes, and one recorded greeting. The maths rarely argues for skipping the announcement.

blocks.quote: Every long weekend, the same three questions arrive on repeat. We finally learned to answer them before anyone has to ask.
blocks.attribution: Aisha, call-desk coordinator, polyclinic group, Muscat

blocks.text: The template that ends the holiday-week complaint

segments.text: Most holiday-week complaints trace back to a vague announcement. "Closed for National Day" tells a customer nothing about when to try again. A usable template names the last open day, the exact reopening date and time, and one route for anything urgent.

items.text: English: "We are closed for National Day from Wednesday 25 November through Saturday 28 November. We reopen Sunday 29 November at 8am. For urgent matters, message us here or call [alternative number]."
Arabic: نعتذر عن استقبالكم بمناسبة اليوم الوطني من الأربعاء 25 نوفمبر حتى السبت 28 نوفمبر. نستأنف العمل يوم الأحد 29 نوفمبر الساعة 8 صباحاً. للحالات العاجلة يرجى التواصل على [الرقم البديل].

Use the same two sentences on the door, in the WhatsApp away message and in the phone greeting, word for word. Consistency is what stops the third phone call asking the same question the first two already answered.

segments.text: If your phone line already runs on an automated agent rather than a fixed recording, the closing and reopening dates can sit inside its answers the moment someone asks "are you open", in Omani Arabic or English, without anyone re-recording a greeting for four days of the year. That is the kind of small, practical use a business that already staffs a phone desk gets from a system built for that desk, not a gadget bolted onto it.

Pick the actual hours for 25 to 28 November this week, not the week before. Write the two-sentence template once, in Arabic and English, and paste it into Google, WhatsApp, your phone greeting and your door sign without changing a word between them.
Afterwards, a call analytics dashboard can show you how many of that week's calls were simply asking about hours, which tells you whether the announcement actually landed.

blocks.title: Your two-minute check
paragraphs: Open Google, WhatsApp and your voicemail right now and check three things: do the hours for 25 to 28 November already appear, does the reopening date say 29 November, and does the door sign match all three. If any one of them is missing or different, fix that one first.

items.q: Should we close fully or run reduced hours over National Day?
items.a: Either works. Hotels and clinics often keep a minimal line open; dealerships more often close fully. What matters is announcing whichever you choose, clearly and everywhere.

items.q: What if National Day shifts closer to the date?
items.a: It has not, for 2026. The Ministry of Labour published 25 and 26 November well in advance, so this is one holiday you can plan without waiting on a late confirmation.

items.q: Is one language enough for the door sign?
items.a: Arabic and English cover most customers. Add a third language only if a regular share of your walk-in customers read neither.

segments.text: National Day 2026 gives most teams a four-day stretch from 25 to 28 November, reopening 29 November. The businesses that avoid a week of repeat complaints are the ones that put the same two sentences on the door, the phone, WhatsApp and Google, days before anyone needs to ask.
